neighbours.label: ' zero' or ' negative' as the level an economic rate or growth figure reaches ('cut rates to zero', 'growth turned negative'); the output promotes ' negative', ' zero', ' positive'
fire: The Bank of Japan lowered its benchmark rate to zero in 1999.
Inflation in the euro area fell to zero in the autumn.
Quarterly growth was revised down to negative territory.
Real yields on ten-year bonds have turned negative.
The retailer's operating margin shrank to zero over three years.
Population growth in the region slowed to zero by 2010.
After the shock, net job creation dropped to negative for the first time in a decade.
Analysts expect earnings growth to stay at zero this year.
quiet: The Bank of Japan lowered its benchmark rate to three percent in 1991.
Inflation in the euro area rose sharply in the autumn.
Quarterly growth was revised up to a healthy pace.
Real yields on ten-year bonds have turned higher.
The retailer's operating margin doubled over three years.
Population growth in the region accelerated by 2010.
The referee showed zero patience with the players' complaints.
She felt negative about the whole trip after the argument.

notes: Probe: rate 'to zero' 0.48, 'turned negative' 0.34, but rate 'to two percent' 0.27 and 'zero tolerance' 0.07: it may be the value slot of a rate more than zero itself.
